:::caution
This rule is part of the [nursery](/linter/#nursery) group. This means that it is experimental and the behavior can change at any time.
:::
## Summary
- Rule available since: `v2.6.9`
- Diagnostic Category: [`lint/nursery/useExpectToHaveLength`](/reference/diagnostics#diagnostic-category)
- This rule has an [**unsafe**](/linter/#unsafe-fixes) fix.
- The default severity of this rule is [**information**](/reference/diagnostics#information).
- This rule belongs to the following domains:
  - [`test`](/linter/domains#test)
- Sources: 
  - Same as [`jest/prefer-to-have-length`](https://github.com/jest-community/eslint-plugin-jest/blob/main/docs/rules/prefer-to-have-length.md)
  - Same as [`vitest/prefer-to-have-length`](https://github.com/vitest-dev/eslint-plugin-vitest/blob/main/docs/rules/prefer-to-have-length.md)
  - Same as [`playwright/prefer-to-have-length`](https://github.com/playwright-community/eslint-plugin-playwright/blob/main/docs/rules/prefer-to-have-length.md)

## How to configure
```json title="biome.json"
{
	"linter": {
		"rules": {
			"nursery": {
				"useExpectToHaveLength": "error"
			}
		}
	}
}

```
## Description
Enforce using `toHaveLength()` to check the length of an array or string.

Checking the `length` property with `toBe()`, `toEqual()`, or `toStrictEqual()` works,
but when the test fails, the error message only shows the two numbers that didn't match.
`toHaveLength()` also shows the value whose length was checked, which makes failures
easier to understand.

The fix is unsafe because `toHaveLength()` fails when the value doesn't have a `length`
property that is a number, and an equality check doesn't. For example,
`expect({}.length).not.toBe(1)` passes, while `expect({}).not.toHaveLength(1)` fails.

## Examples

### Invalid

```js
expect(files.length).toBe(1);
```

### Valid

```js
expect(files).toHaveLength(1);
expect(files).not.toHaveLength(1);
expect(files.name).toBe("report.txt");
```
